REVIEW: 차를 타고 우도를 돌다보면 나오는 산호해변입니다. 일반적인 해변과 다르게 오밀조밀한 흰색 산호가 인상적인 곳! 물도 진짜 에메랄드 빛입니다. 꼭꼭 들러 보세요.

우도 선착장에서 차로 5분도 안되는 매우 가까운 거리에 있으며, 해안길을 따라 산책겸 걸어가도 그다지 멀지 않은 곳에 있습니다.이 해수욕장은 모래가 아니고 산호 조각으로 해변이 이루어져 있어 색다른 풍경을 선사하는 장소입니다. 그래서 서빈백사라고도 불린다고 합니다. 하얀 해변과 파란 바다의 조화가 너무 아름답습니다.주변에 상점이 몇곳있어서 먹으면서 산책하기도 좋은 곳입니다. 우도에 가신다면 꼭 들러보세요.
유일한 단점인 가는 길. 고불고불 하고 돌길이라 타이어 펑크날까 조심조심 가야해요ㅠㅠ 목장에서 파는 우유 요구르트 너무너무 맛있어요.. 아이스크림도 짱이고 체험도 진짜 재미있었어요 기억에 오래오래 남을듯 !

가족들과 함께 하는 6월말 제주도 여행 중에 오전에 아침미소목장을 방문하였습니다덥지만 날씨가 맑아서 좋았던 거 같아요기본적으로 카페가 있고, 송아지들에게 우유를 줄 수 있는 체험존 그리고들판(?) 느낌의 너른 잔디밭과 목장, 예쁜 사진을 위한 포인트존 등이 있어요우선 송아지에게 우유를 주는 체험 학습존은 매우 좋았어요4살 아이라 조금 겁내기는 했지만 책 속에서만 보던 송아지를 보고직접 우유를 주는 체험은 재밌게 했어요카페에는 송아지에게 주는 우유를 비롯하여 치즈나 요구르트 같은 유제품 그리고커피 등을 판매하고 있습니다젖소들이 뛰어다니는 들판 느낌의 넓은 목장이 있어요 스팟 자체가 넓어서참 시원한 기분이 들어요사진 찍기도 좋았던 거 같아요!~ 군데군데 사진을 찍기 위한 장식물이랑 포인트 공간 등이 있어서 젖소들이 있는 목장과 하늘을 뒷배경으로 사진 찍기도 좋구요교통은 대중교통으로는 가기 어려울 듯 해요 가기를 원하면 렌트를 해야 할 거 같고6월말에 같은데 덥긴 했습니다참고로 오전 11시 전에 방문했는데 그 때는 입구 주차장이 한산했지만 정오가 지나니주차장이 꽉 찬 상태였습니다 공간 자체가 아주 넓은 편은 아니라 이동 포함해서는 반나절 정도, 목장은 한 시간에서 한 시간 반 정도 사진 찍고 체험하고 차 한 잔 마시기에 좋은 스팟 같아요사진찍기를 좋아하시는 분들은 가시면 후회는 없을 듯 합니다~

It was at the end of Hamdeok beach. It is not too high and easy to walk. I loved the view from the hill and you can see hallasan from seoubong. If you are staying around Hamdeok beach, seoubong is a great place to see sunrise or sunset. I loved it!

DRAMA WORLD is consist of DRAMA STUDIO, TEDDY BEAR and WEDDING PHOTO ZONE. Drama studio is an indoor exhibition hall with a floor area of 5,000 square meters. Drama studio is actual TV drama studio and restored studio in KOREA, USA and EUROPE, in which the visitors can experience all costumes and accessories for free(except HANBOK, Wedding dress). Our exhibition is consist of town(street) studio and interior studio. Our exhibition is consist of Korean studio(K-DRAMA) and World studio(USA,EUROPE DRAMA). Visitors of all age groups can experience KOREA culture, Western(USA) culture and The Middle ages(EUROPE) culture through DRAMA STUDIO. We are the first experiment-type drama studio in Korea where the visitors wear the costumes and use the articles to be the main character in dramas. ※ Now, World Studio is consist of TEDDY BEAR EXHIBITION and WEDDING PHOTO ZONE with a background of Western and The Middle ages studio. Collaboration between DRAMA WORLD and TEDDY BEAR. TEDDY BEAR Exhibition Hall’s floor area is about 1,000 square meters. At DRAMA WORLD, visitors can see TEDDY BEAR, which produced scenes in drama of Korea, USA and Europe. Visitors can easily understand the scene of drama. Because the text(Chinese, English, Korean)is placed in each display of TEDDY BEAR. Visitors can take a picture with man-sized TEDDY BEAR using props and wearing costume for free. Visitors can learn about the Self-Wedding culture of Korea through the Wedding photo zone with a background of drama studio. Visitors can take a picture in wedding photo zone on studio of the Western Age in USA, the Middle Ages in Europe and Korea’s drama. In each Wedding photo zone, wedding accessories are placed. And they are available for free.

Il faut vraiment être un connaisseur de l'histoire coréenne pour venir ici. Mais même sans l'être c'est intéressant, en particulier si on s’intéresse à la calligraphie chinoise. .L'accès est gratuit.Peu d'explication en anglais.
제주시에서 약 80km 가량의 거리.오후3시, 혼자서 택시를 탔다. 약 35,000 원.도착한 곳은 주차장.약 5분 걷고, 추사관 도착.박물관 가이드의 친절한 설명과당시 상황을 보기에 충분한 1시간여추사를 상념하였다.당시 거주했던 초옥을 재현한  멋진 곳도 보고 앉았다.비오고 바람이 세게부는늦은 봄날.. 멋진곳을 다녀왔다.강추.
TV프로그램(알쓸신잡2)을 따라 가보게 된 곳입니다. 추사 김정희의 유배지와 남긴 작품들을 감상할 수 있습니다. 해당 프로그램을 보고 가면 더 의미가 깊을 것 같습니다.엄청나게 볼 것이 많은 곳은 아닙니다. 역사적인 장소나 기록에 관심이 있는 분들에게 추천합니다. 건물음 ‘세한도’에 그려진 그 집 모양으로 건축되었습니다. 느낌 있습니다~

귀양으로 서귀포 대정으로 내려와 위리안치 형을 받았다고 하네요. 알쓸신잡에 소개된 뒤 많은 분들이 찾아오시는 것 같습니다.추사의 세한도에 나오는 집을 본따 만든 건물이며, 지하로 되어 있어요. 건물 뒷편 지상에는 추사가 유배와서 지내던 집이 있고요.추사관 내부에 전시된 것들은 대개가 영인본이나 탁본이네요. 유홍준 선생이 기증한 물건이 많습니다.가이드 투어 시간도 있는 것 같으니 참고하세요.

We went to the memorial hall to see the exhibition on Kim Manduk after we visited a recreation of her travellers' in that is about 150m away.I have always admired Korea's efforts to recreate buildings and scenes fron the past that are both infirmative and interesting.The exhibit at the hall added to what we had learnt at the inn.What comes across from the information cards and exhibits was a woman dedicated to the service of others.Profit was never her main motive. Nor self-aggrandizement.We need more people like her today.

Kim Mandeok Memorial.I really liked this place personally. I came to know of this woman, Kim Mandeok from this memorial museum. She was the first CEO woman in Chosun Dynasty, which was quite unusual especially as a woman. And when a famine came to Jeju, she helped people in Jeju. Because of the benevolent act, she was still remembered even now. Even a Korean drama dealt with her life. Her life is very exemplary and inspiring. You can find a fraction of Korean history here.

This is for the female Merchant who saved people in Jeju island 17,18 Century, Joseon dynasty. Very carefully and beautifully made. However, it is limited for 3rd floor. 2nd floor is for kids' experience museum. 1st floor is for some special exposition from time to time. It is FREE, worth to visit for an hour. It is located near by Jeju coastal international port and Dongmun traditional market. Actually from this market, exit/entrance #3, it is just 500 m away. In those times, people in Jeju island could not get out of the island, however, since she saved whole population in the island, The King Jungjo wanted to give a awards but she refused. Instead, she asked him she would love to visit the peninsular once, and wanted to travel in Diamond mountain(located in North Korea now). So she could get the chance to meet the King and travel inland. Under the Patriarchal system, it must be very hard for her to work as a merchant, but became the most rich person in Jeju, then when there was big famine, she released whole rice and food for free to Jeju people. Any way, it was great fun to enjoy each section from her birth to death. All explanation are in English and in Korean both.

We wanted to visit an orange, (tangerine) farm in Jeju, where the famous Jeju oranges are grown.Through the tourists information centre, we found this farm nearest from the city centre. We had to take a bus.It is a very nice orange farm. Fee is 5,000₩ per pax- with unlimited time, eat as much oranges as you want while in the orchard & get to bring back 1kg of oranges at the end of it.Great deal considering 1 small tray of oranges in the markets are selling for same price or higher.The young lady in charge was very friendly & helpful although she don't speak English ( Google Translate comes in handy everytime ).The shop was very nice too. Products made at the farm using their fresh oranges includes jams, confectionery & oranges as well. The small production factory could be seen from the shop.Free tasting of their orange jam plus few pieces biscuits included. The jam was very good, made of real oranges.

Abu Oreum was a great easy hike.  Took about 45 minutes to get to the top, hike all the way around the crater, and get back down with a 5-year-old and 7-year-old walking.  There is a trail into the crater that we didn’t take.  The climb itself from the parking lot to the top is less than 10 minutes. Has beautiful views of the countryside around it and a very pleasant walk past some cows and a small forest. It was also very easy to find and park.

When visiting other countries I realize the treatment of animal standards may differ, but I at least look for animals to be happy. This falconry “center”was bittersweet. Some of the animals had wonderful enclosures, but the birds of prey were treated very inhumanly. The same birds of prey/owls were tied to stands for the whole 3 hours we were there, with no food or water, in the blaring sun, with no supervision as people crowded and tried to touch them to the point they would flinch or try to fly away, only to be yanked by their chains. Their inhumane treatment brought tears to our eyes. At the far part of the center, we came upon their enclosures, cages about 5 x 5 x5 feet wide, where other birds of prey were chained, with little place to move and absolutely no enrichment toys.  This is unacceptable. There was a raccoon in a small enclosure with no enrichment toys, solely used for tourists to take selfies with. Last but not least, a pair of Coaty were also in a small enclosure. Their baby was on display in a small cage by the gift shop with no water. This “Center” does have some acceptable enclosures for fowl, rabbits, budgies, and the alpaca interaction was amazing, but surely they can treat all their animals with dignity. While we were there, a macaw flew away into the surrounding trees. Clearly the parrot did not have an attached handler nor proper training for flighted birds.
What a cool find we only knew about because of a brochure from our hotel. So many different animals to see and we even got to touch and feed some of them!

Bonte Museum was designed by Tadao Ando who designed scores of museums (including the Suntory Museum in Osaka) in Japan so the building itself is very photogenic.  The complex is divided into five galleries with one of them permanently housing two works by Yayoi Kusama, Pumpkin and the Infinity Mirrored Room (each visitor gets two minutes inside).  One gallery is dedicated to Tadao Ando’s meditation room while the rest of the  artwork inside rotates.  The other three galleries were pretty bland with one dedicated to Korean traditional crafts and the other two dedicated to temporary exhibitions.  Each gallery is relatively small with the entire museum taking a little over an hour to check out.  The spacious surrounding area is a nice spot to chill after checking out the art if the weather is nice and despite the steep admission, it was still a worthwhile stop.

I was really impressed by this museum, designed by the famous Japanese architet Tadao Ando. The architecture of the building and the beautiful garden make this place worth a visit, but the collection is also really interesting. I really loved the collection artefacts from the late Joseon period an the special exhibition 'Carriage to Heaven' that shows sangyeo (traditional funeral bier) and kkokdu (small statues used as decoration for the sangjyeo). The joyous artwork of Japanese artist Yayoi Kusama were a nice extra on top of all that.Not to be missed when visiting Jeju.

This is an excellent museum featuring contemporary art as well as traditional art. The buildings themselves, which were designed by Tadao Ando, were amazing. It was great just walking around inside while perusing the exhibits & or going for a stroll outside. My favorite part was the sculpture garden, which featured 3 pieces. You can go on the rooftop as well to see another sculpture as well as a great view of Jeju. I was also fortunate to have an opportunity to see Yayoi Kusama's Pumpkin & Infinity Mirrored Room. I don't know if it was because I went during off-season, but the museum wasn't crowded at all, so I was able to take my time. I would definitely come back here again if I had a chance
Outstanding art gallery, with excellent exhibitions and buildings, nice café, an absolute must during your stay in Jeju!
Really enjoy my time here at Bonte Museum, quiet, quaint with lots of funky modern art displays from indoor to outdoor, all my pictures taken there look fantastic from every angle.
simple & peaceful environment. not too crowded & good for taking time for scrolling. staff also professional & nice with good communication.

I had a lot of fun riding the carts but also enjoying the beauty of Jeju. It's situated in such a beautiful location where you can view the ocean and take Instagram photos! The interior of the building was also cool. It was futuristic and very clean. The staff were friendly and helpful! I didn't play indoor games but there were many indoor games as well, so it seems like a place that you can have fun in any season. I will definitely recommend this place for any ages!  I will go back in a heartbeat when I visit Jeju next time!!
Excellent place. Lots of fun and great staff. The staff were helpful. Very efficient, clean and reasonable place for family and friends.

I'd highly recommend visiting 9.81 Park on your next trip to Jeju. This place is a lot of fun. The karts are in excellent condition, the course offers some amazing sea views and the staff are very professional and helpful. Definitely worth a visit.
you can teach or give information how the engine and model grow from old to modern system. and also they have an simulation driving licence for kids .Kids will very like it

Although they say no phototaking but trust me, phototaking opportunity are plenty once u r out of their sight. Read that there's an outdoor area where we can feed the deer. Unfortunately it was raining shortly after we were there. Hence didn't manage to do there. This place is very near to the ossulloc green tea museum. Easy to swing over after the visit to ossulloc. But beware to check weather. There's a unsheltered slope uphill from the entrance area (remb to bring enough umbrella for whole family in case it rains). My hubby only brought 1 from the car hence he needs to go bk to the car and climb uphill again just to pass us the ponchos and umbrellas). :P

REVIEW: This place is amazing! I expected to find something of this quality in the US or Europe, not on a vacation island in Korea. The cars on display were absolutely amazing and gorgeous. Classic cars for me are better than modern machines as they have more unique designs and just invoke a more awe inspiring feeling within. Absolutely love it!
ADDRESS: 제주 서귀포시 안덕면 중산간서로 1610 세계자동차 제주박물관

REVIEW: Couldn't believe that a car museum of such excellence would be found on Jeju Island in South Korea.the large number of cars covered all makes, types and brands and we just loved all the old advertising posters around the museum.The displays outside were also a delight and the museum was not hard to get to by public transport.  We stopped off to watch some of the races on the way back and that is also worth a visit.  They use descendants of the Mongolian ponies, and with their colourful jockeys they made a wonderful display.  The extensive grounds have lots to entertain children as well as a mini golf course in the centre of the race track.  Would definately recommend both destinations.

REVIEW: You have to walk on a ramp in order to get into the museum because car cannot drive into the area of exhibitions. The venue is separated into indoor and outdoor. For outdoor exhibitions, you should be aware of the weather. If it rains, the ramp would be slippery, so visitors are recommended to wear water-resistant shoes for unusual events. There are plenty of cars exhibited, including antique cars and modern cars. There are descriptions beside every single car including where they produce, which car firm belongs to and when it is first produced. There are many limited-edition cars and some of them are even the only one in the world. There is also a shop located besides the entry of the museum, selling different car models and peripherals. I bought a wheel like key chain, it costs 10k KWD, which is relatively cheap compare to the models of cars.So, if you are a car fan or you want to have some souvenirs about cars, you are recommended to go to the car museum to buy your favorites.

But they had a Bentley and a Chevvy so I'm more than happy.

Sammu Park is a destination not likely to appear on the typical package-tour’s itinerary for Jeju Island, but this downtown Sin-Jeju gem has some singularly unique features for the intrepid visitor.  First, the park was actually constructed on one of Jeju’s 368 oreums, local dialect for a small scoria (cinder) cone or parasitic/parallel volcano.  This one is Beduri oreum, surely one of the smaller ones, topping out at just 10 meters above its base with a circumference of 617 meters.  Beduri was transformed into the park in 1978 as part of an urban planning initiative. In addition to a large assortment of exercise equipment,  a children’s play area, badminton and basketball courts, and jogging/hiking trails, Beduri boasts a majestic, two-story octagonal pavilion, called Sammujeong.   Constructed in the traditional Korean style and ringed by pine trees, the colorful wooden pavilion is almost like a giant tree-house.  It isn’t unusual to hear musicians and vocalists practicing there, taking advantage of the spot’s natural acoustics.  It’s a peaceful place to sip a beverage in any season.  Next, are you a train enthusiast or history buff?  Then you might want to visit Sammu for this feature alone:  the park is home to the last remaining steam locomotive for coal transportation in Korea.  MIKA Steam Locomotive No. 304 (registered Cultural Heritage No. 414) was manufactured in Japan in 1944, during Japanese colonial rule, and operated on Korean railroads until 1967. In 1978, President Park Chung Hee had it shipped to the park on Children’s Day, so that Jeju’s children could see a real train.  The train’s passenger car now contains a children’s library.  Finally, beginning in 2014, the park has been further renovated to be a sort of extension to the Bao Jian Street tourism and shopping district.  At the park’s south entrance, there is a giant clock surrounded by wildflowers and neon lampposts that match those on Bao Jian.  The clock has a Plexiglas dome that gives its neon face a trick-art, psychedelic look after dark.  Sammu Park is definitely worth a visit, particularly if you are staying at an area accommodation or if you will be going to Bao Jian…a chance for a little Jeju “nightlife.”

one of the best Art museums on Jeju island along with Arario museum, a moment of calm and meditation around one of the great modern Korean artists

Kim Tschang-Yeul museum had a stylish exterior designed by Tadao Ando.  Featuring the namesake artist Kim’s sculptures and paintings, the museum is very chic for a government run museum. Kim’s trademark is the water drop, which is added to what would otherwise look like rather plain patterns painted on canvas.  The sculptures mostly contained large glass water drops.  Some of the outdoor sculptures complement Ando’s architecture very nicely.  This was an unexpectedly cool visit.

As I've mentioned on my review to Seongpanak Trail, I'd recommend it as the point of entry then exit through Gwaneumsa Trail. But, if you prefer a more challenging option, do the other way around. I went down from the summit through the Gwaneumsa Trail. It was the first week of April and the snow hasn't melted completely yet, making it slippery. It is very much recommended to have a walking stick, in my case, I used my tripod. The scenery in this trail was awesome. There are valleys in yellow and white. You can also find a spring water along the way. Hiking Hallasan in general solo is not a problem, regardless of which trail you take, because there are a lot of other hikers you meet along the way.
Part of Hallim Park. Your entrance fee to the park grants access to this site. Nothing special, but already included, so check it out. Easy to go thru, even for the older less mobile people.

Eoseungsaengak adalah puncak terpendek dari beberapa puncak bukit di gunung Halla atau disebut Hallasan. Buat orang tua atau yang tidak kuat jalan jauh, jalur ini cocok untuk didaki karena jaraknya hanya 1,3 Km dari gerbang masuk Eorimok atau 2,3 Km dari halte bis. Bila musim dingin juga turun salju seperti puncak lainnya. Jalurnya sendiri tidak terlalu menanjak dan sudah ada treknya sehingga tinggal mengikuti saja. Waktu tempuh ke puncak sekitar 30-40 menit saja dari gerbang masuk.

The bridge during night time was nice. I saw this on the plane from Seoul to Jeju. At first I came to see the sea next to it, but then I suddenly saw the bridge and thought it looked beautiful. It really brightens up the dark.
The lonely tree is a amazing place for taking photos, due it's location in a vast landscape is a good place to take photos and explore the beatitude of Jeju.
단풍이 귀한 제주도에서 가을 놀이 할 수 있는 몇 안되는 곳. 제주 시내에서 한라산 쪽으로 15분 정도 걸림. 주말에는 무척 붐비고 입구 근처에 주차장이 있지만 복불복. 한라산 둘레길이라서 여유가 있다면 걸어가도 좋다. 건천 계곡이라 돌맹이가 험하니 5세 미만 아이는 동반이 힘들 수 있다. 10월말-11월초가 단풍 절정.

My visit was in the mid-afternoon, and there were only a handful of casino patrons inside this small casino.When you enter the casino, they ask for your ID, and then they make a photocopy of it. I do not believe that there is a legal requirement for them to photocopy your passport (or in my case, Korean residency card) for their permanent records. Frankly speaking, I was offended by this requirement. To check a visitor’s identification, yes; permanent photocopied record, no.I had the intention of playing some blackjack, but as soon as I saw that they use continuous shuffling machines, I walked out. It is impossible for a blackjack player to gain the tiniest of advantages when such machines are used. My recommendation to blackjack players: don’t waste your time going to this casino.

C1 ( 2016.07.13 ) This museum was meaningful museum of Jeju's anti-Japanese. This museum's outside had monument, square and sculpture about anti-Japanese. The museum was not bigger than I think, but there was operating about 10 years, and had meaningful exhibits. That's good to visit bright attraction in Jeju, but I think this meaningful attraction was good to visit sometimes.
the flowers really pretty and the property is huge, each room was different and i loved it, only thing was it was sooooo hot!!

I've never imagine that I could spend 3 hrs for a botanical garden and that will be not enough :)The garden is very well and smart planned! Such many things to  see inside and outside of main tower!2 hrs is an absolute minimal time to spend there! Some small shops with hand made decorations and one or two coffee shop are inside of main building.Possible to "rent" a small funny train for to travel around of territory - but in this case just not possible to see and feel every perfect corner of the external garden as the train is going by schedule and route.

The place was small, there weren't many things to see and entrance fee was insanely expensive at 10,000₩ for an adult. Not a recommended place to go, best to go elsewhere like the waterfalls or jusangjeollidae rocks.

We decided to pay a visit whilst we were on a weekend trip to Jeju as my wife loves flowers. She was not disappointed!The display of orchids, her favourite, were quite spectacular whilst we were there.

Fall season would be dull here. We made a stop on the way to lunch. A few exhibition halls to cater for vegetation from different temperate and climate.  Otherwise, nothing spectacular in this huge park. The train ride requires a special ticket.

I was very excited to visit after reading the reviews; while it was very nice, I left slightly dissapointed. Maybe we visited at the wrong time of year, but almost nothing was blooming outside. The different outdoor gardens were pretty, but I was expecting a lot more colorful displays.Inside was a bit more of what I expected (although again, not as many flowers as I thought there would be). The main area is air-conditioned, which is a HUGE relief from the heat outside (and some of the display rooms are pretty toasty, as well).  We were lucky to get a clear day, so the view from the top of the glass dome was fantastic.The garden is in a great location, with plenty of restaurants and other attractions nearby, and just a short drive from Pacificland and the beach. As a stand-alone, the garden may have been a bit of a let-down, but since we were able to spend a couple of hours here, get some lunch, and then head down to the beach for some waves, it ended up being a fun family day.

There is a huge greenhouse with 7 separate areas of different plants including desert, aquatic, floral, jungle, and tropical fruit.   The tropical fruit area had platters (examples)  of many different types of the fruit of the nearby trees.   There are a couple small shops in the greenhouse selling different items as well as food and drink.    There is also an elevator going up to a 5th floor observatory.   We went on a very rainy day.    Couldn’t see a thing.   The greenhouse was extremely busy, I’m sure moreso due to the bad weather.      10,000 won to enter.

I was thinking of skipping this attraction in favour of the natural attractions. Due to bad weather I visited this place on a whim but I enjoyed it better than expected. The building itself is quite pretty like a big greenhouse. The floral arrangement and landscaping is tasteful although not as good as Gardens by the Bay in Singapore. There are pretty sculptures dispersed through the compound. There are many different gardens to explore. We visited the indoor gardens first followed by taking the lift up to the top floor for a view of Seogwipo and lastly took the train for the outside gardens. It was too cold and windy to walk outside. There was some confusion about where to buy train tickets, the driver helped to walk to the counter and buy our tickets. Spring is probably a good time to visit since many flowers are in bloom. It would be good if they can stop the vandalism of the trees by the Koreans, many of them scratched their names on the branches.

Easily accessible by public bus from airport! This garden is not so crowded & have nice decoration so can relax. Locals like to visit this place & not foreigners are seen during my visit there. Next to this garden have a waterwall so got another place to relax. Recommend to go teddy bear museum & kpop museum as very near to one another so this will spend one whole day.

Lovely botanical garden. I went there a couple of days ago with my friends during our Jeju trip.We didn’t want to get around the whole island for the short holiday, but relax. There were a number of flowers, trees, flowers, and beautiful gardens.If you are a fan of gardens or nature, you must visit there.
I loved the indoor botanical garden. The greenery was so uplifting away from the cold winter outside. There are many species of plants and the gardens are themed from desert to jungle to fruit etc.

If you love nature, then you absolutely must visit this place. According to the booklet I took, there's an outdoor and an indoor garden. The latter one has 5 different sections: a flower garden, an aquatic garden, a cactus garden, a jungle garden and a tropical fruits  garden as well as an observatory on the 5th floor.The outdoor garden contains TEN different gardens including the herb garden and a french garden. It would take about 2.5 hours to see everything it offers.TRANSPORTATION:-from Jeju: take the Airport Limusine Shuttle (approx 50 mins)-from Seogwipo: take a public bus (approx 20 mins)

We visited here as part of of our cruise ship day tour of the island. This is a very pretty place with amazing photo opportunities throughout. We purchased one of our favorite souvenirs from a kiosk selling genuine Jeju produced hats. We enjoyed the gardens and the walk over the bridge with the amazing views of the gorge and waterfalls. Be aware that the VERY long walk down to the "close-up" of the waterfalls is rather taxing and may not be worth the effort. Overall, a great experience!

What a fantastic place to visit, spectacular looking ,inside ,jungle,cacti,gardens under glass ,lift in the middle at the top you get to see all gardens outside you can explore,the beautifully Italian and French gardens are just so awesome,well worth a visit ,although yes extremely hot,lots of Aircon outside garden areas ,cafe to cool down .

My wife and I went to this place all of a sudden as We had no plan to cover this area. it is located in Jungmoon Resort area. the environment is like slience is spekaing everything. alongside the three water falls are awesome. Go and see.

The indoor gardens are very lovely especially the flower and cactus gardens. We were there on a sunny day in May and expected it to be hot inside. But these are not just greenhouses. They are greenhouses with air conditioning and so it was pleasantly cool and we took our time to walk around and admire the plants in comfort. The gardens are very well maintained without a leaf out of place. The arrangements are very pleasing and and these two gardens are simply beautiful. Go on a sunny day when the light and shadow creates a most charming effect.As for the outdoor gardens, the Italian one is very picturesque with a magnificent water feature. This is not so much a garden but nonetheless very attractive.Definitely worth a visit.
The inside is beautiful but had a huge amount of school groups which made it hard to walk around. The outside gardens are lovely and romantic and makes for a nice stroll with your significant other.
The outdoor gardens lack maintenance and looks nice from a far but is very bad when up close. The plants are balding and the fountains are empty.
This was one of the nicest gardens I have ever seen. Beautiful 5 rooms with different items there. Nice observatory.
It is worth to see this. You can see 5 different gardens with different themes. It is nice for children and for adults as well.
It was enjoyable to walk through this botanical garden,  but I have seen better. It was great fun to go up to the top of the tower for a 360 degree view of the area.
We visited Jeju in the off season so the outside wasn't what it normally is, but the inside was absolutely beautiful.

This is a beautiful place to learn about the gardens and native korean plants.  There are many different types of gardens here and they are all well maintained and interesting.  You could stay here for a long time just learning or you could breeze through casually enjoying the scenery.  There is a tower you can go to the top of for lovely views of the area.  Bring a water bottle.

This botanical garden is well arranged, it enables you to travel around the world through its flora. Pleasant warm ambience, pretty flowers, trees and plants, outside garden too. Great for sunny days - you can admire the view of Hallasan volcano.

The cone-dome architecture is interesting, the roofs of different gardens within culminates to a peak into the center of the compound and u can take a lift up to catch a 360 panoramic glimpse of the surroundings (see pic). However, adult tix are at 9000krw per person which is not cheap for what u get within. The place has lots of potential but not that well-maintained as the place looks very weathered on the whole. There is a garden dedicated to tropical fruits but those are mostly common fruits for southeast Asians like us. There were only chrysanthemums at the entrance even though it's supposed to be in-season. Parking is easy though, and free, like most places of interests at Jeju. Overall, this place is more suitable for the elders and for people dropping by to visit Cheonjeyeon falls and Seonimgyo Bridge, which is just next door. Otherwise, my 2c worth - it'll be fine to spend your money elsewhere.

The gardens were reasonably well tended and we liked the indoor themed zones spreading out in a cartwheel from the main atrium. Outside there are a series of larger themed gardens. Some better than others, but it is a South Korean take on these different countries garden styles. For example the fountains in the Italianate garden were quite impressive and it was good to stroll in the sunshine. We did like the many sculptures placed within the various indoor spaces and this has lifted our score from 'average' to 'very good'.

The Yeomiji Botanical Garden is easy to find and has parking places available. Entrance is not so pricy. The place is easier to enter with stroller or wheel chair. The glass house is quite big and divided into flower/aquatic/cactus/jungle and tropical fruits garden. The outdoor garden is also spacious but we did not go there. Not many people have visited the place. Consequently it was quiet and empty. The garden is very beautiful, interesting and green. It has also a lot of plants and trees but the wow effect is definitely missing.  On top of the glass house is also a view point with elevator connection. Finally I have seen much better botanical gardens.
Enjoyed a comfortable tour of the gardens. Has lots of plants, flowers and trees from all over the world. It is is just beautiful.

Pathetic and unkempt..it is a disgrace to call this place a "botanical garden"! The so-called Korean, Italian and French Gradens were not even kept up! The interior greenhouses were a waste of time! It is a absolute waste  of money!

I love nature so this place of course was one of my favorites.  I wish I could upload videos on TripAdvisor.  I can during the fall season and was blown away, imagine what this place looks like during its prime time, spring.  Anyways, must visit here, must.

It wouldn't usually be my first choice to visit on an island filled with so many views but it was a rainy day so it seemed reasonable. Wasn't disappointed. The indoor exhibition is well arranged and themed: there was jungle, desert, and other sections. You can climb to the last floor of the tower in the middle for a nice view of the area. Can't go wrong in any way if you stop by. Didn't see the outdoor gardens since it was pouring rain but wasnt disappointed even with the indoor one alone

The building itself was amazing and the indoor gardens were impressive. You can take an elevator up to the 5the floor lookout for a nice view through windows that need cleaning. The outside gardens were mixed. Japanese garden was the nicest overall but smaller than I would have guessed. The Italian and French gardens were impressive by scale alone but the details were far under kept. Green water, weeds??? And I between the larger gardens were under kept areas like a  garden that looked lame at best.  With all that it was still worth a quick stop but don't get your expectations too high.

I am used of the garden by the bay in Singapore which is great, so I went there just to depend some time and expecting something just .. so so.I was actually wrong. The garden is nice, outside as inside. The round shape with all kid of plants, the elevator to go on the top and enjoy a great view, the type of gardens outside (japanese, coréen, italien, french...).Sometimes a lack of maintenance but.. definetely a nice place. Entrance is about 7usd for adults. A little train can bring you around but I didnt use it and.. not sure it is free.

The garden starts with a huge glasshouse which is a torture in the summer but we went anyway on carpe diem basis. It's awesome inside and it has little sections. Then outside there are European Japanese and Korean gardens with walkways. Coming from Europe I was not really amazed or entertained by the eurogardens but I guess with Asian perspective they were impressive. The reason I gave 4 is that the entry is expensive and they only sell water at 1 place. Also the toilets are quite dirty

the indoor as 5 themes each of them very tidy and pretty. the exterior has different zones and a large lawn. i went there thinking just another botanical garden but i was well impressed i recommend.from here you can have a nice view from the entire red bridge and from the top of the indoors garden you can have a 360' view from entire city and surrounds on a clear dayreally worth to visit

You need to pay an entrance fee which doesn't include the train ride (which is an additional small fee if you opt to use it). The train can take you on a short ride to view the gardens. Inside the greenhouse, it's quite warm and you can climb up some stairs to view Jeju Island from the top. There was some renovation being carried out in the lifts.  Can spend 1-2 hours here if you're not a garden fanatic!  It's located next door to the Cheonyijeon Waterfall.

The greenhouse structure and the design of the gardens were very nice.  However, it seemed that the staff was having trouble keeping up with it.  It may be just a bad time of year for them.  Still well worth the admission fee.
Close to hotels - a very relaxing place to wander around and enjoy. Peaceful and friendly for all ages

The entry fee is abit on the high side, but if you love gardens, plants, nature, and especially flowers, it’s worth every penny. My absolute favourite place to visit in Jeju. I love flowers so we spent around 4 hours here. There’s a huge variety of flowers, and the gardens/areas are very well laid-out. Besides the greenhouse, there is also an area outside where all the different-themed gardens are (Korean, Japanese, French etc), there are about 12 gardens in total I think, and all of them are really beautiful. I think this attraction is still relatively new, as I could still see gardeners setting up the flower beds and so on. But this also means that it’s not crowded yet and there are relatively few tourists compared to the other attractions. Flower-lovers, this is a must-visit!

Maybe in the spring or summer would be better but it was really badly maintained (rusty lamp posts, signages, litter all over floors, shrubs and ponds) really sad. Don't waste your time or money (9k won per person) coming here.

I love botanical gardens and this one is good-lots of different themed gardens which are nice to wander around and explore. You can also stumble onto the view of the nearby bridge which I have forgot the name of but it was near the French garden. There is also an observatory which you have great views of all over Jeju including Hallasan. Lovely way to spend a few hours.
This place is full of colorful flowers, plants, trees. Various catagories of plant life, a scenic place.Really liked it.
Wonderfull Park! If you visit Jeju Island, i recommend you to visit Yeomiji. A lot of themes. So many places to take a good pictures.
I came here without any plans. It was better than I expended. The warm house is beautiful and elegant. Must go up to the roof and you can see the astonishing view!!!

At first, going through the green house,  we were a little disappointed until we walked the grounds outside.  The French  and Roman gardens were absolutely beautiful.  It was so peaceful and relaxing.

I wouldnt get out of my way to visit, but if you are in the area and enjoy gardens, you might want to visit.Outside, the japanese and korean gardens are lovely. The french and italian gardens are too kitschy for my taste. Inside, the water flower garden is especially nice. Make sure to take the elevator up to the "observation platform" -  if the weather is clear, you can get good views of Hallasan.

Yeomiji, located in JoongMoon sightseeing complex, is one of the most impressive place in my memory. - Entrance ticket fee is under 10USD, which is quite reasonable. - Area is divided by its own theme like tropical, Japan, Korea ... - Why don't you order a cup of coffee(or ice cream) and take a rest at the center of greenhouse garden- Observatory has nice view. but it is easily get crowded.Tip: you'd better to go CheonJeYeon waterfall(천제연폭포) after here. that place also has beautiful natural scenery :)

The weather was raining on the day I decided to do sightseeing on Jeju, so I was left with only a visit to the botanical gardens. You can reach it from the airport limousine bus route and behind the fast food shops near SK Energy shop.Luckily the garden exhibition was under glass roof, so it provided a good informative shelter from the rain.The botanical gardens are organised into themes, eg. Aquatic garden, cactus garden, etc. I guess this eliminates confusion for tourists and displays the plants in an educational fashion too. On a sunny day, there is more to do on the outside.There is a curio shop inside the gardens for some gifts but I did not see a coffee shop at the attraction.It will be educational for the kids!
Whether you like flowers or not this worth a visit as they have loads of different flowers from around the world.

The indoor gardens are great when the big rains come.  Went back the next day and enjoyed the outdoor gardens as well.  Unfortunately, there is a person screaming via a loudspeaker at the entrance, which spoils what could be a peaceful, serene experience.

My wife and I thoroughly enjoyed our time at these gardens. The effort that has gone into creating different exhibits both indoor and outdoors in extraordinary. It has an extremely relaxing feel and a great view of the volcanic mountain.

Beautiful indoor gardens with several rooms leading off of main garden with specialized environments. The rooms leading from the main garden that I can recall right now are a tropical plant room with orchids, a fern room, water plant room with lilies and hyacinth, and even a cactus room. It is a large indoor garden with many colorful and unusual plants to see. It was raining the day we were there so we were happy that it was enclosed. There are beautiful Korean and Japanese style gardens, among other types of gardens too, outside. Jeju Island has many beautiful places to visit and this botanical garden was a great excursion for us.
Beautifully laid out. Many different styles of gardens, all beautifully maintained. The class house houses a fantastic variety of plants from all around the world.

The botanical garden is a place where a wide variety of plants are displayed for understanding how vast is our plant kingdom.it may also help to understand the geographical peculiarities of different countries all over the world. The best thing I have seen there was they provided each species scientific details along with the source country. It will be so exciting to see our country plant representing in a botanical garden situating in a foreign place. Furthermore botanical garden is situated in a very beautiful place with a wide variety of gardens and trees, as I said earlier all the plants and trees are named perfectly.

The garden has probably seen better days, as some of the facilities look worn down. However, the plant life is beautiful and healthy. I enjoyed the cactus garden the best. It was a bit pricey for what it is. I’d recommend seeing the natural attractions instead.

Here you can find a lot of beautiful flowers and tropical flora. It is very suitable for green lover. Besides, you can find some tropical fruits over here with some information. After visited four themed garden park at the ground floor, you may proceed to the top floor using the lift at the center. You can see the beautiful view at the top floor. Also, you can take a train tour outside the building. :)
There are pretty parts to the garden, but it's definitely not worth the 9,000 won entrance. It's very stereotyped. Hallim Park is far better for a half-day trip and a similar price.
It's nice very beautiful inside and out, one of our favorite place some of our best pictures together taken here.
Zoned gardens, lovely to stroll about and inside the dome was quite unique. Also an excellent view from the top of the dome.

The Botanical gardens is set up in to different gardens and a large doom/ indoor area set up into zones. The plants on show were very nice but I have seen a lot better. This could be because of the South Korea climate. Look at the surface and it's well kept then you notice dirty water in the ponds. What I did enjoy was watching some of the workers weed some of the areas they are so methodical. As we were part of a day tour this was just one of our many stops and our time was limited. Perhaps I would have enjoyed it more if I didn't have such a tight schedule. I would rate this attraction as Good but there isn't a good rating and average would do it a disjustice. I thought the entrance fee to be very high considering the country it's in. You don't pay much more to go in Kew Gardens, London's Botanical garden that can actually take you days to get round.
Great place to enjoy walking and see different species of plants, trees, we enjoy palms, something special, very quiet place

For a rather expensive entrance fee of KRW9,000, was somewhat disappointed with what it offered. Basically, the park is divided into 2 main areas, the inner garden and the outdoor garden. The inner garden is essentially the large glasshouse, with different sections of the glasshouse each housing a different theme, i.e. cactus garden, flower garden, aquatic garden, etc. In the centre of the glasshouse, you can take the lift / stairs to the top, where you can get a panoramic view of the entire estate. The sight was rather impressive, but the glasshouse did not seem to be maintained well. The outdoor garden is basically the land around the glasshouse. It is divided into various gardens with different themes (i.e. Korean, Japanese, etc.). In general, they were rather uninspiring and gimmicky. The French Garden was ok, but like the rest of the park, didn't seem to be maintained very well.There is a train that goes round the garden but when we tried to board it, we were told that we needed another ticket. Quite disappointing after having paid a hefty entrance fee. We decided to just walk instead.All in all, the park seems past its prime, and maintenance could have been better. I'd imagine that it was quite grand when it was first built.. especially the glasshouse.
A lovely place to visit with lovely areas for all types of visitor. Especially family friendly and particularly beautiful first thing in the morning.

For those who loves nature.. This is where you can see plants you've never seen before. The area was so huge but it did not deter us from walking and exploring. They kids also loved the exotic plants and were excited to see the carnivorous plants that were indoors.
This garden was well maintained with a wide range of flowers, plants and cactus. Relax and take a slow walk to admire the surrounding. A nice attraction not to be missed if you like garden.

The park is divided to theme gardens from different areas (China, Japan, Italy, ...) Huge greenhouse has tropical fruit in glass domes so yo can learn how cocoa and bananas grow. There are also glass-fibre dinosaurs and crocodiles hiding in some of the more jungle-like parts. From the viewing platform you can see all the gardens and surroundings. Place was a must-do for schools trippers, who were plenty when I visited. A relaxing stroll in beautiful surrounding.

I would not call it a must see attraction, but go there if you have spare time. I really liked their collection of cacti and insectivorous plants. The glasshouse arrangement is really impressive. The tropical section had fruit-bearing mango trees which was a sight to behold (inside the glasshouse). The French garden, the Italian garden, etc are good for a stroll. Didn't find anything there specifically impressive.
Every theme garden was in the peak of health and beauty.Allow several hours. Inside and outside gardens.Great view from the top of the tower.

8000 KRW for entry, it makes Yeomiji one of the most expensive attractions on Jeju Island. The Italian Garden was a laughing stock and several of its gardens are in a terrible state.The only redeeming attraction of this place is its glass dome which has tropical gardens etc. However, if you are on a short trip in Jeju, you should give this place a miss and go see some real nature outside.

Shows good selection of plants from various regions. Good organization of displays. Conveniently located near Hotel. Provided relaxed pace in touring the place. But limited information provided on plants.

This was one of the only attractions that was open the day after Typhoon Bolaven moved away from Jeju this summer. On the day after there was still some strong wind and it was overcast, but people were out clearing debris off the roadways and sidewalks. Our hotel called ahead to this Botanical Garden and they said they were open, so we took the bus over and sure enough it was! It was a huge greenhouse building with an observation area at the top you can climb stairs to and see all over the area including the ocean. There were different climate areas inside with plants from that part of the world (jungle, dessert, local climate, flowers, etc), a small cafe with coffee and ice cream, some shops, and restrooms inside. Outside there were nice grounds with a big grassy area where people could sit, and other themed gardens (Korean, Japanese, French, Italian). Very pretty. Signs inside in English and Korean and Chinese describe some of the plants.  There were lockers inside for rent with coins. They weren't huge but we saw some backpackers taking a medium sized pack out of one.They were renovating part of the building but we didn't smell or hear anything bothersome. All in all it was a nice place to visit if it's raining or just post-typhoon outside, if you love plants, or have some extra time to see sights on Jeju.

I love visiting botanical gardens whenever i travel.  Unfortunately this is one of the poorer ones and I feel compelled to warn others!  With an entry charge of 7000 won per person, the value is low.Let's start with the greenhouse, it was just ok, nothing exciting.  During sunny days, the greenhouse is like a toasty oven as the ventilation is poor.  There is a variety of plants but they are not well organised or well kept.  Moreover, if you live in tropical parts of Asia, you would have seen most of the fruit trees and plants in neighbourhood backyards, which makes visiting it less exciting.Besides the greenhouse, there are themed areas - e.g. Korean garden, Chinese garden, French garden etc.  I was excited to see these options but after seeing what there was at the Korean and Chinese gardens, i just gave up on the rest.  I don't have the confidence the others will be worth the time.Management of the garden needs to be improved.  When I was there, they were renovating the entrance to the greenhouse.  As a result, the smell from the paint, varnish or whatever that toxic smelling thing is, is overwhelming.  Also, there was lots of noise.  Garden management would have better managed the renovation or at least inform visitors there is renovation going on.  I tried to offer feedback to the folks at the ticket counter on my way out but they didn't seem to care.In summary, there is nothing much to see and the garden is not well taken care of (even if there is no renovation going on, I would have rated it 'Poor').  Go to this place only if you have nothing else to do.The only plus I can think of is ... parking at free!
I was fortunate enough to visit in the middle of summer on a beautiful hot day.  Very romantic and pretty.  A peaceful place which appeared to be very popular with a large number of tourists.

The garden is huge and beautiful. Unfortunately, it was a rainy day when we visited the garden. Different variety of plants from different part of the world are collected in a dome. A full tour throughout the dome takes around 90 minutes. There is also an observatory above the dome for people to overlook the Jungmun Tourism Complex. Though the garden is huge, I found most of the plants are not native to Korea. It is a pity that foreign tourists can not know more native plants  by visiting this garden.
This botanical garden is a great place to learn about the local flora of Jeju and Korea.  The entrance fee is quite reasonable and there are lots of places to eat both inside and outside the garden.

There really isn't much flora and fauna (this was in March) to speak of. Even indoor plants don't seem to flourish. The only nice thing about this place is there is a big park in which you can lie down on and enjoy the sun!
불행하게도 제철에 간 게 아니라서 그냥 들판? 허탕만 치고 온 느낌이었습니다. 검색하다가 사진보고 간 곳인데, 2월에는 영 실망이었습니다.
길 양옆으로 유채꽃이 피어있어 제철에 가면 드라이브할 때 기분이 좋습니다. 중간중간 차를 세우고 사진을 찍을 만한 포토 스팟들도 있습니다.
제주도 동쪽에서 제일 큰 규모의 핑크뮬리 카페가 생겼다. 정원카페인 글렌코는 10월 방문하면 아름다운 핑크뮬리를 만날 수 있고, 겨울에는 동백꽃이 있다. 오픈한지 오래되지 않은 곳이고, 카페 입장 시 1인당 1음료수 주문이 필수다. 음료수 가격에는 정원 입장료가 포함되어 있는 셈이다.
There is no infrastructure and lifesaver all around. Good for walk at sunrise or sunset with nice in any direction :)
Great view of Soengsan Ilchulbong.  Beach changes colour from black to brown to yellow. There is aslo a small seafood restaurant with great food.

We were there in mid-March, hoping to see the mossy beach of Gwangchigi. Sadly we were out of luck. It was high tide then. But still the sunrise view was breathtakingly beautiful. Would certainly come back again to see the moss. Anyone knows when is the best time please suggest. Thanks in advance!
This was a stop on our Yeha bus tour - East Course - we stopped for maybe 15 - 20 minutes and it was a beautiful spot to take some pictures and see Seongsan Ilchulpeak.

Went there to watch sunrise with Sunrise Peak background and foreground with water and rock.  The beach is large and we could find a spot without disturbance of others.  However, there is no official car park space.

Gwangchigi Beach is hours of fun for the whole family; at low tide! My son (6yr) learned to navigate the moss on the rocks within minutes. No one, I repeat no one, got hurt. There was bird watching & go figure snail finding. An excellent morning/day/night.

Its a relaxing to catch the sunrise here best if you have rented a car. There is also a coffee van which will be there around 6am. you can get yourself a hot drink or quick breakfast if the cold winds of the morning gets you!

I chanced upon this wonderful beach along Ilchul-ro Road while my family and I were on our way to Breeze Bay Hotel. I returned to the beach in the late afternoon and my family and I went to the same spot again the next day early afternoon. On both occasions, I parked our car at a car park that’s got just a few cars. Gwangchigi Beach is very long and the spot that I was at was near to a erected stone put up by the Rotary International. The good part was that there were very few people on this secluded beach. The better part was that Gwangchigi Beach is a black sand beach (yes, we finally experienced a black sand beach). The best part was the beach offers a marvellous view of the south-western face of Seongsan Ilchulbong. Using a pair of binoculars or a telephoto camera lens, you could see visitors climbing the stairways as well as the summit of Seongsan Ilchulbong.Moreover, walk along the beach and you will find unusual rocks and rock terrain just beyond the black sand. I believe the rocks arose from the explosion of an underwater volcano long time again that created the Seongsan Ilchulbong. During the late afternoon or sunset, the sunlight produced a beautiful array of black, brown, orange and green (algae-covered) colours of these rocks. Because late afternoon is where low tide occurs, the sea water was trapped within the rocks as ‘ponds’ – and there were beautiful reflections of Seongsan Ilchulbong on the still water. Alternatively, you could walk on the rough brown ‘mat’ (not sure what’s the material) that was laid on the grass. It was along this mat path that I saw a horse that was tied to a pole. I guessed the horse was used for horse-riding but I didn’t see such activity as it was already past 5 o’clock in the afternoon.Gwangchigi Beach is one beach in Jeju that is under-rated and not well known. It warrants being among the top 10 beaches in Jeju. Anyway, I recommend visiting it as part of the Seongsan Ilchulbong experience.

Gwangchigi Beach is a beach near Seongsan Ilchulbong.We park our rental car on the side road.There are a few cars & tourist bus park along the road.We can see beautiful view of Seongsan Ilchulbong from this beach. The beach is long and it has black sand.The beach is unique to it own because of the green stone/rock at the shore.It produce picturesque photo because the green stone contrast with the blue sea.This beach appears on drama Warm & Cozy starred by Kang Sora and Yoo Yeonseok.

약간의 경사길을 따라 걷는 것은 다른 오름과 다를 바가 없으나 끝부분에 도착하면 숨겨진 장소처럼 푸르고 평탄한 초원이 나타나서 놀라운 곳입니다. 오름을 가면서 강아지를 데리고 오신 분이 많아서 무슨 일일까 했는데 나중에 숨겨진 초원을 보고 나니, 이곳에서 강아지들 뛰어놀게 해주고 싶어서 데리고 온 것 같았습니다 (물론 목줄은 다 하고 있었음) 치마를 입고 데이트 분위로 오신 여성분도 많이 보았을 만큼, 산책하듯 걸어다닐 수 있는 곳입니다.

My friends and I pirposely went to this theme park as we are fans of the Bae Yong Jun drama- The Legend, when we planned this trip, we asked the tour agency to include this on our itinerary. The facade was like a fortress from the Joseon dynasty except for the cars in the parking lot, the ticket booth and te posters saying this place was the location for the drama " The Legend" with a big picture of BYJ. We feel like we travelled back in time, the entrance is the main village with the bridge and man-made lake, the houses are surreal as you can see inside its like 3D not only the facade of the house then as you turn right you will see the village for common people , its more hanok styles, there is a market place with plastic meats, beefs but lloked real and the center of the village has a big traditional bar , it has second fllor where you can go up and see the view of the rest of the village, there were chairs and tables with some traditional glasses and wine bottles where you can do some photoshoots, there were tradional rickshaw downstairs, and a well with water, then there's a big gambling house with tables, some traditional games, with a big wheel with numbers you can bet on it, then a high ranking official house where you can go inside, there were furnitures, a fire place, there's living room, bed rooms and a TV where the drama is being shown, they really used this for the drama, thenat the center if the whole theme park was the big palace, as there were big gates leading to the palace with the whole field with cobbled stones, the palace is just so surral, you can enter it, you can see receiving rooms for the royalties, the emperor's chair, the rooms for the royalties with huge bed, books made of bamboo so it looked like window blinds, then there' s a roomfilled with hanboks where you can wear them and take pictures with it, there were mannequins of the characters in the drama, there's a dungeon too where they filmed the slaves or criminals being  punished, there were other rooms as well like the dining room with huge and long dining table, ere's a garden too with waterfalls, whoa! its really like the whole Joseon dynasty vibe! We took a lot of time taking pictures of the whole place with every nook and cranny of this place, its really a place for those who are fans of the drama or BYJ or even if you are curious how they live during those times, its like we time travelled back to those kings, emperors, slaves, scholars. the entrance fee to the park is USD10 and you can stay as long as you like. We used a private car courtesy of our tour guide but its quite far from the city as I remember we travelled for at least an hour from our hotel Shilla,but its worth it.

As the name implies, this street is a street of restaurants & dining. There are so many "nice" appetizing looking  restaurants as we explored the place.A very helpful "road map" at the main road entrance shows the restaurants names & types of food & exactly its location within the street.This street is nearby Seogwipo Maeil Olle Market. Seogwipo main town is quite small, so most of these "attractions" are quite close by.

There is a secret bunker at on Jeju Island, which once housed old national communication facility and had remained unknown to the public for a long time. This large structure is covered with soil and trees, thus disguised to look like a mountain. This old national facility will be reborn as “Bunker de Lumieres”, a media art exhibition hall that will become Jeju's new landmark for culture and art.

Bunker de Lumieres is a bunker with the images of the works by the featured artist projected on all sides of the walls.  The display alternated between 30 minutes of Vincent Van Gogh works and 10 minutes of Paul Gaugain.  The images were absolutely stunning and it didn’t take long to get into an almost hypnotic state staring at the moving images.  The calm music playing enhanced the experience.  The Van Gogh part was definitely more entertaining because of the familiarity factor.  Other than the relatively remote location along with the steep entrance fee, it was a worthwhile visit and a unique way to appreciate some well known fine art.

t's really nice here. I didn't expect much from my mother even before I arrived, but it was really good.  Gogh and Gauguin's works are reconstructed  with light. And I didn't realize the time was passing. If you have a chance, go there!
Thoroughly enjoyed this gallery. Visually spectacular especially with accompanying music. A very different way to view art.
Very well put together with a fantastic collection of music which really compliments the art making it a fully immersive experience. Well worth a visit.

Don't miss this show if u are in Jeju. Only available & performing until October 2020....awesome immersive show.  @ 빛의 벙커 Bunker de Lumières. The floors and walls become the canvas of this highly immersive digital art that come to life, as Van Gogh's art work are displayed all over and synchronised with beautiful clasical music. Definitely worth the more than an hour show.We enjoyed it tremendously!

Entrance was KRW15,000 which was extremely expensive for the show. There are simply not the facilities here to walk with the number of visitors and the parking is extremely limited so you have to park on the main road and walk quite some distance to reach it.  Expect no support from staff in any language except korean.

The experience is new and the music is nice. However, I go bored after some time because I am not a art person and do not quite grasp what the artists are trying to express. Driving through narrow road to get there.
제주도 지도에서 찾을 수 있는 동굴이지만, 학술적인 이유로 인해 관광객들은 출입이 금지된 곳입니다. 입구에 서보면 시원한 바람이 나온다고 하는데요 어차피 찾아가봤자 철망으로 봉쇄된 입구밖에 볼 수 없으니 찾아갈 필요는 없습니다

세계자연유산으로 등재되어 있지만 일반인은 출입이 금지되어 있습니다.거문오름 국제트래킹 기간에만 입구까지 갈 수 있습니다.이곳 앞에 서면 에어컨보다 더 강한 바람이 붑니다.특별개방되는 용암길의 일부로 쉬어갈 수 있게 통나무 의자가 비치되어 있고쉬어가는 사람들은 시원한 바람에 매료되어 쉽사리 일어서지 못합니다.개인적으로 너무나도 보고 싶지만 어디까지나 욕심이고 하나둘 사람이 늘어나면 훼손되는건 시간문제, 그래서 아쉬움을 달래봅니다.입구까지 본게 어디냐~

This is the second time my family and I have visited Gapado Island since we had a good experience during our first visit back in November of last year. Unfortunately, our image of Gapado overall is now completely ruined due to an extremely unpleasant experience at the restaurant named “Gapado Yonggung House” (가파도 용궁정식&민박) Upon arriving at the port at Gapado, we saw many restaurant advertisement posters. We found one restaurant poster with nice food images, so I called the restaurant to get directions. The owner (male) who answered the phone was quite unfriendly and told me bluntly to just look them up on naver map and find our way. He said that even if they give me directions, I wouldn’t know they are located. So my family and I found our own way to the restaurant after a 20 minute walk. It turned out that this restaurant was located furthest away in Gapado Island. We ordered our meal and started to set our own plastic ware. Due to Covid-19 sensitive period, we always bring our own disposable chopsticks, spoon and paper cups to restaurants. The owner (lady) out of the blue bluntly asked us if we bought our own cups in a rather accusing manner. We said yes we brought these cups and asked “why do you ask?”, to which she said “Oh, we have some cups in our kitchen and wondered if you took them” I found this question to be rather offensive as I feel she was insinuating or implying that we just took (or stole) them from their kitchen without their knowledge. However, we overlooked her strange question and went about eating our meal. We then wanted to order soft drinks. However, I could see that all staffs, owners included looked quite busy. Therefore, in my attempt to be helpful, I went to the fridge and removed two soft drinks from the fridge while at the same time informing the owners of my action of taking the 2 drinks, to which they acknowledged. To be perfectly clear, I was telling them to charge me for the 2 soft drinks I was taking. However, only a few minutes after this action, I overhear the lady owner speak to her employee in a very loud voice to not stock up the fridge with so many soft drinks because people keep taking them from the fridge, while she herself was removing half the stock from the fridge and putting them away in the back storage. At that moment, I felt she was saying this intentionally to let me hear her, as her way of telling me that she was not pleased with the fact that I have removed the 2 soft drinks directly from the fridge. So at that point, I told the lady owner that I wanted to clarify that when I took the drinks from the fridge, I was telling her to charge me for it and that it didn’t feel nice to hear her make that comment so intentionally. This is when we have experienced the most horrifying and unnatural turn of events. The lady owner got extremely angry at me and started yelling and shouting at me saying that she wasn’t talking about me, that she was talking about her other guests, etc. She could have very easily cleared up my mis-understanding in one nice sentence. Rather, she was ready to bite my head off and was talking (more like yelling, shouting) at me ten times louder than my voice. I was so shocked by her behavior that I said I just wanted to clarify any potential mis-understanding about my taking the soft drinks, which I was telling them to charge me for, and that I actually did that as a gesture to be helpful since they looked so busy (obviously a huge mis-judgement on my part).  The lady owner would not let this go and kept on yelling and arguing with me, her voice escalating louder and louder every second. I told the owner that we took the time to visit their restaurant and did not appreciate being treated like this. To this comment, the male owner jumped in and said that fact has nothing to do with this matter. Neither the lady nor the male owner offered one single word of apology nor made any attempts to provide explanation for their rude behavior, nor try to rectify this intense situation. The lady owner having her say just ran off and hid in her room after having her furious tantrum with us. Although extremely disturbed by what just happened, as we have never experienced such rudeness ever in our entire lives, we still managed to complete the remainder of the meal in silence, all the while feeling ill at ease and uncomfortable. (FYI, my entire family and I suffered from indigestion later this same day due to this incident). After the meal, I paid for it at the counter and left the restaurant with my family, and not one single person at the restaurant acknowledged that we were leaving their restaurant, and no one (owners, staffs) even bothered to say a simple “thank you or goodbye”. I am a firm believer that the most important part of any meal at any restaurant is quality of service. However, the level of horrible service we have experienced from this restaurant is completely unacceptable. From the many restaurants we could have chosen from at Gapado Island, I certainly feel choosing this restaurant is the one mistake I will live to regret. This unpleasant and rude encounter was bad enough to leave a bad image of the entire Gapado Island for us, while at the same time ruined a perfectly peaceful and happy family trip. If it’s springtime—or even summer or fall-- that means it’s also time to think about visiting beautiful Gapado, or Gapa Island, which sits just off the southwestern tip of the Korean resort island of Jeju.   Located some 5.5 km (3.42 mi.) offshore, Gapado is a quick ferry run from the port village of Moseulpo (maybe 20 min.)Gapado nearly got the distinction of being South Korea’s southern-most point, but that title went to nearby Marado.  Some tourists want to go there just to say they’ve been, but Gapado is noteworthy in its own right.  Gapada is home on its .84 sq. km  to about 250 residents.  The island has a picturesque school, a church and a Buddhist temple.  There are a couple Korean restaurants and small stores.  But, it’s a good idea to take bottled water and snacks with you, particularly if you plan to hike or bike all the way around the island.  You can bring your own bike, or perhaps rent one there.  Walking (Gapado has a 5k hiking trail that is part of Jeju’s famous Olle Course) or biking/electric scooter likely will be your only transportation choices, as there are no fossil-fueled vehicles on Gapado… But more about that in a bit.What makes it so special there?  Gapado offers spectacular views of the iconic mountain peaks or “sans” back to the north on Jeju, including Sanbangsan, Gunsan, Songaksan, Gogeunsan, Dansan and the Big Daddy of All Sans, Halla…the massive, central shield volcano that formed Jeju Island and the highest peak in South Korea.Equally impressive are Gapado’s golden-green barley fields, surrounded by traditional “batdam” stone agricultural walls.  The crop begins sprouting in late winter and reaches its full glory in late spring.  Gapado’s tradition of barley cultivation dates back to the 1840s and is celebrated annually with the Gapa Green Barley Festival. (Dates for 2015 are April 18- May 10.)Back to that transportation thing…well, barley is not the only thing green about Gapado.  Wind turbines, solar panels and other renewable, sustainable forms of energy are now being used on the island as part of a plan to make it one of the world’s first carbon-free islands, maybe THE first…. Summing up:  Good points:  outstanding natural beauty and photo ops in all directions; fresh air; clear aqua-hued seas that reveal black lava rocks; abundant hiking; colorful neighborhoods festooned with murals, recycled art and traditional Korean cultural artifacts;  site of annual Gapa Green Barley Festival  (April 18-May 10, 2015)Be sure to have on hand:  bottled water and small snacks; comfortable shoes; sunblock;  sunglasses; and a hat that won’t blow off easily; a stroller for very young children, layered clothing for coolish days.  There is little shade on the island, so be on guard against dehydration or sunburn on those hot or even excessively windy days.  Getting there:  Take an Intercity Bus from most points on Jeju Island to Seogwipo Main Terminal, and from there, a local bus to Moseulpo .  There is a short walk to the ferry from the busstop.  Ferries generally run twice a day, but as schedules and fares can change, it’s probably best to check for specifics through the Korean Travel Hotline: dial 1330 in country or outside Korea: +82-2-1330 or 1339 (Korean, English, Japanese, Chinese)

On Jeju Island's Halla Mountain--at 1,950 meters, South Korea's tallest-- can be found Korea’s highest paved roadway, known as 1100 Meter Road or the 1100 Highland Rest Area.  There, you can take a self-paced nature hike on an elevated wooden walkway through a “volcanic” wetland; with its many lava rocks, trees and wildflowers, this place has an otherworldly beauty that you and your camera will love.  You’ll likely see lots of ravens, magpies and maybe some roe deer (be sure to stay alert for them along the highway if you are driving). Across the road, there’s a colorful café and shop, offering local beverage favorites and snacks, as well as souvenirs.  (They carry a good selection of galot clothing, made locally using persimmon-dyed fabrics.)  From the café’s observation deck, enjoy a perfect view of some of Halla’s most famous landmarks, including Yeongsil Folding Screen Rocks and the 500 Generals Rocks.This area takes on a very different character with each season, and locals often drive up to see the magnificent ice formations that form on the trees and rocks in the winter and spring, when Halla’s higher-elevation trails may be closed to hikers.  But it’s also a good choice for visitors who have limited time to climb, even when the higher trails are open, because it is possible to experience these incredible scenes at the 1100 Meter Road area.Not only is this a beautiful area, these days the 1100 Meter Highland is part of the Jeju Biosphere Reserve, a UNESCO and World Natural Heritage Site.A couple of points:  this attraction is actually located on Highway 1139, which will also take you past Eorimok, Yeongshil and Mysterious Road. You can drive or take an intercity-bus from either the Jeju City (north) or Jungman Resort area (south) side.  If you take a taxi, you should make a roundtrip reservation, allowing 1-2 hours there.  It’s a good idea to take at least a light jacket, even on a summer day, and for late fall to late spring, have a heavier coat, gloves and even a hat.  And don’t forget your shades and skin protection; even in winter, the sunlight can be strong on Hallasan.

Ce site permet de voir l'empilement des différentes coulées de lave qui se sont échelonnées entre 22.000 et 17.000 ans avant notre ère. Les coulées donnent parfois naissance à des formes curieuses ; elles contiennent également tout un inventaire de pierres et de coquillages. L'eau qui s'infiltre dans la falaise ressort à sa base sous forme de mini-fontaines. D'après la légende, ces fontaines représentent les larmes d'une jeune fille pleurant la mort de son frère, tombé de la falaise après avoir tenté d'y cueillir des herbes médicinales pour guérir sa mère gravement malade.
