I crossed the Believe it or not museum many times, in New york, in Baltimore.. but never stepped in.Finally I tried the one in Jeju island and I really liked it. It is certainly similar to the others, but if you never visited one... who cares?I imagined it small but it took me 2 hours to do everything. I mean... read all, not just give a look and say : oh.. ok!It costs 10usd per person. Expensive or not depends of you.If you are curious and love to travel and discover... it is nice place.

If you like silly things and interesting historical facts check out the museum. It was worth the visit for me as I enjoyed myself quite a bit. There were also some sections for modern history and more tech-based stuff for my partner!

C1 ( 2016.07.13 ) The museum's theme was various and unique. Maybe there was like "Guinness Book". The exhibits was good and arouse my interest, but the price was higher than I think. There was good place to spend killing time and need to increase contents.
the museum is ok, but not what is in there you can find it elsewhere in the world, nothing amazing making worth the journey.

Saw this impressive bridge from my hotel window and was really curious to check it out as it has strong resemblance to the Dubai icon the Burj-Al-Arab. The ocean views are amazing and bridge leads to a beautiful small island. Must visit place if you are taking the trip on the Seogwipo Submarine which is right next door.

We made a wrong turn and found this place by chance.  Amazing view. The bridge connects you to bird Birds Island. It's 1.2km walking path. Best to visit before the Sunset and you will be blown away with the views around this area. A good place to stroll and relax.
NIce  walk across the bridge facing the sea on one side and port on the other .Bridge connects Seogwipo Port to Birds Island and its design is inspired from the Jeju traditional log boat- Tewu

The bridge is in vicinity of my guesthouse and also the Cheonjiyeon waterfall that we visited before the quick stop. It was around sunset when we arrived there. There are free parking onsite. The bridge itself is just average, but it was a nice stroll to Saeseom Island.

Short walk to cross the bridge while having a good time to enjoy the scenery. Nice to take a good shot. One facing the ocean and open sea, while the other side facing the sea with the city as the background.

This bridge connects Seogwipo Port to Birds Island and its design is inspired from the Jeju traditional log boat- Tewu.The best time to view this bridge is in the night. One can walk around the bridge and enjoy the scenery during the day and early evening.
A great view for sunset and at night, you can see the lights being light up at the Bridge with difference colors. Mainly place for you to take pic =)
Well maintained. Excellent view. Get a coffee and take a stroll. On a windy day it can be very cold there.

Walked to the bridge as it was near my hotel (M stay hotel seogwipo). It's a nice bridge and you can walk across it to saeyong island, where you can have a short hike around the island. Nice views during the hike where you can see the ocean and three different islands. It's also near Cheonjiyeon waterfall.

We walked from our hotel located at the Arang Joeul Street to the Saeyeongyo bridge for almost 30 minutes. There were many locals visited and walking leisurely there. There many restaurants and the Seogwipo Submarine was located on the way there. You can see the beautiful ocean wave along the way to the bridge. The bridge connected to the Saesom island. The island was brighted by light and old korean song music at night. We visited the bridge twice in the evening to see the colourful light and daytime to observe the surrounding scenery. The trail to Cheonjiyeon waterfall can be found  on the way to the Saesom bridge. The entrance to the waterfall was after Chilsimnigyo bridge.

The island was teeming with dragonflies and it felt like something out of a Disney film. At any rate, if you are in the area visiting the nearby waterfall, or going on a boat or submarine trip, it is a lovely walk with spectacular views all round.I wouldn't suggest going here specifically, but if you are nearby..... it's worth a look.

Looks like the Burj khalifa of Dubai but its just much smaller and in fact not a hotel but a bridge. Going across the bridge you will be on a small island to walk which will take around 45 min. Great for a scenic walk close to the city. You will also have a good view to the sea and of the diving women of Jeju.

This is a great spot to take photos and there isn't much crowd there. When you walk up the bridge, it leads to a small trail around the island that it is connected with. Take a short walk around the island. There is a well paved pathway for you to walk on.
This is a really beautiful pedestrian bridge to get to a small island for hiking trails.   There are a number of spots for getting great pictures of this bridge along the coast,

This pedestrian bridge leads you to a small island where you can take a walk for around 30 minutes. There is not much to see on the island itself but I will say the view is quite nice. I visited around sunset time but it was a bit gloomy that day so we didn't get to see a nice sunset. There were many mosquitoes when we walked around so beware when you visit during Summer. Otherwise, this is a nice place to spend your time.
This is the place to see sunset.  There is also an easy hiking trail nearby which can be covered in less than 30 min
My 10 yo old daughter and I went to the falls nearby and stopped by here and took some pics. Can definitely get some great photos here. Must see!
A nice evening walk at sunset.There were many locals lying down on the benches, playing loud music.  Although it lacked tranquility, we found it interesting to observe local customs.
We went to this after our Seopwipo Submarine tour.  Very relaxing to walk especially early in the morning or at night.

This was our last stop in Jeju. We arrived right after sunset and were able to walk around the island and enjoy the beautiful nature area and then walk back over the bridge while it was lit up. Good activity for young children to just get out and run. Best of all it was free! There is also a free public restroom in the parking lot.
You can have a relaxed stroll over the bridge and on the route around the Bird Island.  Nothing spectacular, but see the coastine and three island out of the city.

The strong wind will surely blow your mind to imagination. As an avid fan of K-drama, I was fascinated by the location and the scenery that  will make a great backdrop to make a movie. It has a great view overlooking the sea and another island near to it.It was Autumn season in South Korea when I visited Jeju Island. If you are going solo, there is a public bus accessible to this place.

We walked over the bridge, it was very windy and we could feel the bridge moving a little which was quite scary but was really nice to get some air. The island was really peaceful and was a lovely walk around. Unfortunatly there was two children with their dad shouting all the way round, we could hear them from the other side of the island so we sat on a bench for a while to wait for them to leave. We went before sunset and saw the sun set, just be careful of mosquitoes at this time as we got bit loads while on the island.

Nice walk across it and seeing the island plus cliff wall and the fishing harbour bay. After the bridge a serenity walk with beauty scenery walk. Use proper shoe for the walk. The bridge also light up at night with colors.

This bridge connects Jeju Island with the islet of Saeseom and resembles an anchored taewoo, a traditional fishing boat of Jeju coming home with a boatful of fish and its wide net streatched.  The name Saeyeongyo means creation of new connections, as it connects uninhabited Saeseom with Jeju.  Come back when it is dark and see the amazing LED light display on the guardrail of the bridge.

We stayed at a hotel along Jungang-ro road, that was near the Seogwipo Maeil Olle Market. From our hotel, it was a 10minutes walk to Geolmae Eco Park. The park led us along Seohong-ro road to Taepyeong-to road (where we passed by Hotel Yeon) where we were able to see the Saeyeong Bridge. After the bridge was in sight, we followed our instinct to the Bridge. There was an ice-cream stall that serve grape soft-serve that was delicious. We made our way onto the bridge to view the pristine bluish-green coastline. After the bridge, there was a short 20 minutes trail that brought you to a rocky coastline where you can view two lighthouses (red and white). You could walk to the white lighthouse on the rocks but at your own risk. There were many locals fishing along the rocky areas too. In short, the trail along the Saeyeongyo Bridge was fairly easy yet scenic enough. We were there on the 22nd of April and the weather was about 15 degree celcius in the day. A light jacket with windbreak will be sufficient. Afterwhich we headed to Chilshimni Poetry Park (which you can view Cheonjiyeon Falls for free) as there was a stairway along the left side of main exit road (where all the tour buses parked, pedestrian walkway path with brown wood). The stairway seemed to indicate going up the the temple. However, we landed in Chilshimni Poetry Park. We took pictures of the waterfall and left Chilshimni Poetry Park to follow the orange/blue Jeju Olle ribbon to Hwangwooji coast and Oedolgae. The orange/blue Jeju Olle ribbon were along the park main road (where Park Sunshine hotel was). You do not need to rent a car. All these could be done by foot. We clocked about 25k steps walking around for that day.

Good for a walk as it is easy walking with limited stairs and if the weather is good, the peace surrounding the ocean views is rewarding. Can be very busy with tourists and if the weather is windy or wet, then find another place to visit. Some small markets  around the area to visit.

Good sight seeing place and jungle trekking. Wear sport shoes for easy walking if you plan to walk "round the sea". Weather was just nice for walking in April. Crossing the bridge and standing there watching the big sea was feeling awesome.

If you go to Seogwipo, you see this bridge a lot on their pamplets and promo stuff.  In the daytime, it is overrun by tourists and loads of them.  At night, the bridge lits up, there is less people and it's quite spooky hiking around the small little island on the other side of the bridge :).  I recommend going at night :)
a casual stroll was good no stairs and neat views ,  a bit windy but okay was pleased we visited here

Well, there has been near our place in Jeju and in our schedule. We could go by walk and bought Citrus fruit in the street, specialties of Island. The bridge leads to the road around the mountain. Can proceed to visit

Drove by this bridge in jeju which has a sail shape like on a sail boat.  Actually fitting since it is over a small Marina.  We were on a day tour of jeju in November 2016 on the way to some waterfalls when we passed this bridge.

It's a nice place for a stroll, especially in the late afternoon or early evening, that's when the bridge will be lighted up. The bridge leads to Saeseum island where you can walk around it and enjoy the scenery
Went there since it was near the waterfall. The bridge is quite nicely lighted up during the night. We were there for 10 mins. Nothing much just the bridge during the winter night.
Probably not worth going there just to do this, but if you are going to the nearby falls or the submarine, then definitely make time to do this too. It is a pleasant, easy walk.
An easy-to-reach attraction that provides not only a fantastic view of the city and port, but also leads you to the island which is worth the walk in of itself.
Nothing very spectacular about the place. But we came to experience submarine with our daughter and it was an enjoyable experience.

The principal purpose of the bridge is to provide a walkway to Saeseom Island. The area close by is great for photography - clean water, interesting rock formations, local flora etc. The circuit of the island is also very pleasant, particularly in good weather.

After seeing the waterfall, my family of four took a nice stroll down to the bridge.  The view in the evening is wonderful.  The bridge is also lit up nicely at night!  Of note, one can get tickets for the submarine or boat rides at this same location.

What a beautiful place! This bridge looks like it is hanging in the air. A short loop around the island offer a lot of bird sightseeing. You can also see female divers at work right next to the bridge.

We were there waiting for the submarine tour and decided to walk over the bridge to kill time, it's actually quite a plesant one with nice view to surrounding area. I think it might be worth a visit if you happened to be around there.

This bridge in Seogwipo harbour goes across to a small island which takes about 20 minutes to walk around.  It is a nice place to go at sunset, there are nice views and many birds in the trees.  Also nearby are the Cheoniyeon waterfalls, and a few shops and cafes.

The bridge is beautiful to look at, and provides a nice walk to an island that provides more opportunity to stroll near the water.  Big tourist attraction, and if you prefer staying away from the crowds, you may not enjoy this.  Great picture taking venue, and it doesn't cost anything, except a little workout for your feet and legs.

The bridge itself is a landmark of Seogwipo, which leads to a small island that offers a short 20-25 mins walk. Not the most exotic part of the city, but nice indeed. My favourite place here however are rocks on the edge of the island, which is off the track, but if you are careful while walking out to the rocks (they are pretty flat and not dangerous at all), it is the best place to relax and enjoy the sea and view.
The view is not bad and you can see many small fishing boat parking there. But really not particularly impressive so I think it can be skipped if run out of time

The Saeyeongyo Bridge is a great landmark here in Seogwipo and looks amazing. The bridge looks most spectacular in the evening when it is lit up in various different colours. This is definitely worth viewing.
I'd recommend you to go at night since it is much nicer with variety of lights.Also, you can walk around tiny island and it takes about 20 min or less.

It's a nice bridge, and takes you across to the little island on the other side. Not really a lot to see apart from passing through the quaint port and adjacent coastline. Would suit you if you just wanted to go out for a relaxing walk along a peaceful area.
Footbridge is of interesting architecture and good photo opp, walk across to the small island and trek around it (about 30 min) to see the sceneries around.
I mean, its a decent bridge if you've got time to kill and want a good view, but I wouldn't go out of your way to see it.

Our family really enjoyed this walk.  It was nice to see the lighthouse and islands around this area.  And when we were there, the brushes were full of beautiful spiders and webs.  Of course, they were far enough away to not bother you.  It was really cool to see.

A good place with nice view of the bridge and open sea. No entrance fees is required and is accessible via public transport and some walking is needed. Restaurants are available within the bridge area and other attractions such as submarine is located just right before the entrance into Saeyeongyo Bridge.
We visited on a particularly beautiful day and took a nice walk to and on the bridge.  There are tours available from the nearby pier and the overall views are wonderful.

This is yet another bridge among the several others you will happen to see in Jejudo. It is not worth a special visit unless you go with the intention of hiking around the island that this bridge connects to the mainland. The Seogwipo Submarine tour starts from the dock located very close to this bridge. So you can easily explore this bridge and the surrounding area if you come for the submarine tour.

The cab driver brought us to this place. This bridge was near to the harbour.Nice place to walk along the bridge where you can enjoy the surrounding. It was very windy where you able the enjoy the breeze. Indeed just a normal bridge but with nice surrounding.

Nothing spectacular, but I would recommend watching the sunset from the bridge if you just so happen to be in the area. It is also a short bike ride away from Cheonjiyeon Falls which is a nice site to visit during the evening.

We came to seogwipo to see the falls and have BBQ. The bridge was close to the parking lot for one of the falls and it is worth a stop to admire views although don't put your hopes up since it is just ok.
This is just another bridge and I wouldn't drive especially to see it but if your visiting the nearby waterfall you should also check this out. It has a lovely view and looks great at night
its just a bridge but over the other side is a nice little island you can go for a walk around,very touristy area.
Just a normal bridge like many others,it's kind of relaxing with a seaview..as it has no entrance fee, it's no harm to come to this place since it is near to where I was staying.

This is a weak but personal reason to visit this bridge, that is to say, it featured in the first Korean Drama series I ever watched. To put it in a nutshell, the guy followed the girl all the way to Jeju-do in order to convince her he was the one for her. The bridge scene featured just after they landed on the island, so it was just nice to see it in person as part of our stay here. There's not much more to say - I guess other people would have other reasons to visit. As a bonus we spotted women divers going out in their gear so that was some cultural aspect to the visit.

When I saw the bridge from the area of the waterfall the pylon looked as if I would know it. The bridge brings you from the harbor to an island with birds. If you walk around 800 m you get to the end of the island, but not where it really ends. If you manage to walk over artificial rocks for another 200 m, you are at the entrance of the port where Koreans like to fish. If you dislike walking over such rocks, a boat serving fisherman will collect you, and you have the opportunity to take beautiful photos of the bridge.If you wish to take good photos, go there in the morning.

It's a large building but light on exhibits, or maybe it just seems that way with so much open space. Several historical and current type aircraft, mostly military, and several interactive exhibits for kids. Nice digital movies and a flight simulator section for kids and adults!

Not so good experience. Reached this travel spot around 330pm and the museum close at 6pm. We struggled if want to purchase the entrance ticket as we reached here quite late. At the end we decided to enter as my son at 4 yo wanted to experience the G Force Plane and we went to the tourist information counter just beside the ticket booth to enquire the last admission. She explained that last trip for the G Force is 430pm and we asked we are bringing our baby along is it okay? She said no problem but limited to 12 persons per trip. We hurried purchase the ticket and when reached there, the person in charge said at least 7 yo to experience the G Force. My son very upset but fine we accepted this fact. Then we went to each theatre and asked if we can join their exhibition hall. All rejected us as they said minimum age to enter is 7yo except for the 5D cinema at any age. I feel disappointed that the information counter never mentioned about the age limit. In fact prior to this JAM, my husband and I did some research at their official website and their website silent on the age limit for these exhibition hall. This museum had a lot of things to see but a lot of the experiences not suitable for us due to the age limitation. I feel disappointed with the information counter with limited knowledge of their facilities and their website. If I have known that I visited this place but my son can’t do anything here he will be super upset, I will not choose this in part of my travel plan. Anyway, the museum had a good food place and there have some history about air plane beside aerospace.
The museum is big enough but boring. They should have more interesting stuffs. Especially more aircrafts.

We visited the JAM (Jeju Aerospace Museum) and it was stunning, I love anything connected with planes or space so I was in heaven, the displays are well laid out and there were so many interactive displays for kids too that it shows that there was much thought in the museum.Not only was it about aircraft, but also about Korea's history of astronomy which was so fascinating that I could have spent all afternoon in this one section, Then we went into the space exhibition and again I was stunned at how much South Korea has achieved. We always think of  USA & Russia as being at the forefront, visit the JAM to have your eyes opened.Wonderful.

Overall a clean, well laid-out museum at a very reasonable price at 9,000won each for adults.- Not as many exhibits as we’ve seen at the Smithsonian in DC or Naval Aviation Museum in Pensacola but still worth the visit to learn about Korea’s aviation history- Placards translated into multiple languages - Korean, English, Japanese, Chinese. - We don’t have kids but it seemed there were a large number of child friendly play and exhibit areas.- On the third floor was a go-cart type racing track and pizza cafe. It was about 30,000won a person so we didn’t try it but it looked cool.- From the 4F observatory you can see Hallasan Mt, the tea fields of O’Sulloc, and Shinwha Theme And Water Parks.We spent about an hour there in total.

A wonderful place to take children and adults can have a good time as well. There are many shows and interactive displays for children to use. They also have crafts for children. For adults they have very informative displays as well as guided tours

Great for kids and students, educative. And interesting . It has some  experience programs - you can travel in space, by air, feel it like your own. Outside park contains planes and helicopters, you can sit in some of them and take photos.

The Jeju Areospace Museum is located SSW of Jeju at road 1121. It is a huge and obvious building which you can not miss. Lot of parking places are available. Entrance fee is quite reasonable. 2 adults and one child for 28k Won. Good and accessible for stroller and wheel chair. Inside there are a so many things to see. The museum is clearly structured and you have enough room and peace. We went there in the late afternoon and only 3 tour busses were waiting outside. So the museum was quite empty which was simply perfect. Very interesting and nice to see and study was the science  room where especially Bernoulli was explained practically very well. Further you have a huge hall with plenty of planes and units/turbines. Other areas showing other planets and space ships and so on and so on. The good thing is you have plenty of room and feel not like in an anthill. Our three years old boy had so many fun and was so interested. Me too of course and even my wife was quite impressed. Outside a couple of more planes and helicopters. Some of them accessible and we had a lot of fun. There is only one minus: mostly missing English explanations. The value vs. money is worse to stop a second time.

C1 ( 2016.07.13 ) I visited there for watching about flight and space. There was a big size than I think, and many aircraft and exhibits about space was exhibited. There was a good place for children to enjoy about space. The museum's construction cost was tremendous, I think. The exhibits was various, but was not inconsistent, so some place was confused.

The museum has many airplanes on display and also an outdoor area where you can walk into the planes.   Very well done, lots of information and displays.   Hands on activities instructions are only in Korean, but easy to figure out.   A steal for the 10,000 WON entrance fee.
The giant Budha is amazing, and so the views of the sea and the city. The temple itself is also beautiful.
Worth the walk to see the cave and also get photos of the ocean from the top.   Be prepared for a few stairs to get to the top.
There is no harm to walk and hike to see the view of coastline and ocean.  The temple is not grand or manificent.  It is hard to hike to the budda in the cave, but you can try.
as my view that was just a traditional temple. seem not too much local at here but part of trekking point on it. the cave Buddha also not special but ok to visit

This was a nice walk up to the top. There's a lot of stairs, but it's not nearly as bad as I thought it was going to be. We went in Oct on a fairly sunny day (temp was probably in low-mid 20's) and you definitely want some water and sunscreen with you. I'd recommend going when it's more cloudy, if you can. There are a couple little shops along the way to the top (the first few levels of stairs, not all the way along) where you can also purchase water, and there is some tasty Jeju orange ice cream for sale too. The views are pretty, as is the temple, and it wasn't too busy when we were there in the middle of the afternoon.

this is a must-see. A temple in the cave made by ancient volcano corruption. It is on the top on the hill. Great views on the sea, pieceful atmosphere. You can drink water from thespring, it is a water from the mountain and it is clean.

A 'must see' place when visiting the island. Lots of small shops around the entrance, a small fee (free if you work on the island), lots of stairs (a fairly tough climb) that lead to a variety of small temples and places to check out. Views are fantastic and on a clear day even better. You can get their by local bus although there is car parking but no 'wheel' access for baby strollers or wheelchairs. The golden Buddha and the drums give you an amazing feeling sitting so high above the surrounding area. Definitely worth it.
Very good place,beautifull,amazing,you won't say sorry if you come here.easy to find it,bus stop in front of temple.

The Sanbanggulsa Temple is located SSW of Mt. Hallasan directly at the coast. It is a very unique and colourful temple which reminds us more on the temple in Taiwan as in Korea mainland. The temple is located just below Mt. Sanbang. We had our junior with us but with older kids it is probably a nice tour on top including the temple. The view from the temple is very nice and gorgeous. Probably from top of Mt. Sanbang even better. The area is quiet and peaceful.  Except the opposite place where noisy  Korean caterwaul being played at a swing boat. The place is not reachable for stroller and wheel chair. Parking place available. Entrance fee is negligible for parking and temple access. It is definitely worth to stop and to spend some time. Religious people are probably also allowed to pray i guess. Doors are open.
Vigorous climb is SO worth the views and forest around you :) Feel as the Buddhists as you turn the drums and go within.

C1 ( 2016.07.14 ) This temple's shape was unique and located in cave. The way to this tempe was about 15 minutes in uphill stairs and had good view. Though it was hard to temple, but after climbing there was good, and could drink mineral water. Sometimes there was no climbing because of bad weather. There was another temple at the entrance of way to this temple, that temple was good and beautiful sculpture. Good place to enjoy temple and view.

The temple complex is structurally interesting because it is spread out on the foot of the mountain. It's not actually very big and not of the structures are magnificient compared to other temples elsewhere, but very nice overall. But the view is really amazing. Look South and you'll see green slopes going down to the sea, look the other way and you'll see behind the temple rocky mountains that almost look like a cliff. This place captures perfectly the contrast between the sea and the mountain, and is very relaxing.

Not just a temple, but amazing views of the coast and water. The temples are free to enter and offer an amazing experience. A must see if in this area. Plenty of drinks, food, views and restrooms. Only con is the steps are not very friendly. We have a 3, 7 and 8 year old. 3 year old needed carried.

If there is nothing else you do go see this temple. It is a sprawling complex that goes all up to the base of the mountain. Along the way if you do hike all the way up to the top, there are signs to explain the legends behind the names of the places you walk and why there is a temple there. But even if you don't it is still an sight to see

Me and my friends really enjoyed our time around the Sanbanggulsa temple and really enjoyed the serenity and tranquillity it provided. The location within the mountain itself is breath taking and it really does give this temple a unique look compared to other temples. The stream that runs down into the cave is incredible and this place allows you to connect with your spiritual side.

It didn't take as long as we expected to get around the temple, but what was there was beautiful. The big bell was impressive, as was the actual,temple itself, but you shouldn't need more than 30-45 mins to see most of it. Worth seeing though.

Nice peaceful place to visit. Came across this place while heading to Yeogmeori coast. Can be accessed from the same parking lot to the coast. If you're driving a rented car you can key in 7942940. Recommend to drive if you are touring jeju.

There are statues of the Future Buddha, Maitreya; Bodhisattva of Compassion,  an outdoor huge Golden statue of Buddha, hundreds of miniature green Buddhas.  If you climb up the 471 steps, you will reach a cave with a statue of the Bodhisattva of Compassion. The tears that she constantly cries for all the pain of this "ocean of suffering" world collects in pools up the stairs below the altar.  Visitors drink it and make prayers before it. If you drink 3 sips of the water, you will enjoy longevity in good health. Great temple to visit.
A beautiful temple for Buddhists to pay their respects. In addition, the view of Sanbangsan mountain is breathtaking from this area.

The temple is at the foot of the Sambang mountain, where you have a choice to scale 400 steps to the mid point of the mountain to see another goddess statue there. A good 30 mins climb up and down at a casual pace with photo opportunities of the scenery.

A visit to Sanbanggulsa Temple was part of one of my favourite day trips in Jeju. It is about an hour west of Seogwipo-si by bus and across the street (albeit a bit of a hike) from Yongmeori Coast which I very highly recommend. Getting to the temple requires a short and easy climb up some stairs where there is a huge golden Buddha, an army of miniature mint-green budhhas, and a gorgeous panoramic view of the ocean and village below. A little further up is another fascinating statue of Buddha in a cave. Overall, this is a nice place to visit and a great opportunity for photography.

This is one of my favorite places in Jeju.  Walking up the steps to the temple you experience one enlightenment after the next.  The temple and the grounds are in immaculate condition, and clearly there is a lot of love and respect which goes into every section.  This is a wonderful hour or two to spend as you are wandering around the island - take your time, don't rush it, enjoy both the temple and its attractions, and the stunning views toward the ocean and the rest of the island.  BTW, this is not an easy stroll up the hill, but not that taxing either - if you have elders, perhaps you settle for mid-way.  if you're young - do the entire journey, you'll never know when you'll be back.

This temple is on the side of Sanbangsan (san means mountain). The mountain is very impressive. The scenery here is spectacular. I highly recommend buying a ticket for not just the temple but also the beach. (Keep in mind that the beach area closes at either 5:30 or 6:00pm depending on the day.)The walk up to the Buddha was nice with great views of the beach as you climbed. But bring bug spray!! I walked away from here with about 12 mosquito bites, because I forgot to put on my spray until I got to the top.After visiting the temple, leave yourself at least 45 minutes to explore the beach. It will take 10 minutes to walk down (and 15 to walk up - the uphill is always worse!). You can walk out along the coastline, and it's very cool. Important note: getting a taxi FROM here is VERY difficult. We were there near closing time, so no one was being dropped off once it was time for us to leave. Luckily for us, a Korean couple noticed our trouble and offered to call a taxi for us. Without them, we might still be there!

The temples and Buddhist statues were gorgeous at the two temples at the foot of Sanbang mountain. The hike up to the grotto is a short 20 minutes, but if you head up in the summer it'll be pretty hot and sweaty, but well worth it. Great cultural trip on any day in Jeju.

This is such a great place!Even if you don't have enough time, you can see a lot.There are few stages and different "yards" to go to.Really peacefull place if you climb few stages up.After going up you can see beautiful view of the coast as well.And the helpful thing is that they have a small shop in front of the temple (downstairs) so after climbing all mountains and the temple place you can get nice drink or ice cream. Also, they have a car parking place.

We felt peacefulness in this place even if it is next to a main road. The entry fee is only 1000 won and clean facilities.From Seogwipo bus station take bus 700 for 1500 won each way.The building in the Korean style are well maintain and the climb all the way to the grotto is a good exercise. The golden Buddha sit up there under the dripping mountain. People collect the water for  believe of power, may be like Christian for Easter water..Well! Each are different, Friday for the Jews, Saturday the Muslim, Sunday the Christians, everyday for Buddhas...

This temple is way up to the top of Sanbang Mountain & is quite an arduous climb although thereare stairs. Along the way, however, are some stops with breathtaking views of the sea & beyond.The temple itself is not that impressive, I was told, so I did not anymore go all the way up.Anyway, there was also a temple below with a large golden Buddha and the view from there was also nice.

Not the best temple but it seems like a real place and is nicely nestled in the side of a cliff with some steeps steps up to the main grotto with a modern Buddha statue in it. Small entrance fee seems worth it but do not expect too much.

It was quite a strenuous climb up to the shrine in the cave at the top. Although it was a very hot afternoon. The views on the way up are beautiful and you can see for miles. Lots of great photos. Places to eat and souvenirs at the bottom near the car park.
It is located   toward Ocean and you can also watch the Dragon head seashore which is impressive. Nice view. They also have small & exotic temple.

Besides the short walk up to the Buddhist cave, there is a lovely temple and huge golden Buddha just up from the carpark. It does cost money to get in but being able to get up close to the Buddha was excellent. And there are nice views of the coast too.

We visited Yakcheonsa Temple on our Jeju Olle Trail Route 8. This temple looks delightful because of its architecture and beautiful surrounding scenery. The views from the second floor were amazing! We even had a chance to ring the bell and make wishes here! A recommended place for photographers to get vivid pictures. You can also experience a temple stay activity in this Buddhist temple.
I've seen many temples around Korea but this was one of my favorites! So spacious and with the best view. The colorful decorations were also so nice.

Yakcheonsa Temple  is a famous Buddhist Temple located in Jeju, a small Korean island south of mainland Korea. It has been built in 1981 by Buddhist monk and has the largest Buddhist prayer hall . and  miniature gold Buddha statues all located on the second floor encased in glass.The main temple has Two -three floors and balconies that overlook a beautiful three-meter-tall Buddha. The view from the top floor facing the sea is awesome.

We really enjoyed our visit. Great view over the ocean. The temple cave was very different. The main temple was beautiful with brilliant colors. We were told that it was built around 1970. Lots of photographic opportunities.We took the bus from Jungman (Bus 282, 202 or 32) and got off at the Jungman High School stop. We walked back towards the Stone Garden and took a right and then a left. Easy walk from the bus stop.

I arrived to this temple because it was on my route between Seogwipo waterfalls. I was amazed. I thought I had seen enough temples, but this was something else. It is majestic with the palm trees and little ponds in front of it. This has been one of my favourite temples in South-Korea so far.

Overlooking the sea with palm trees this temple is like no other. The surroundings are just beautiful. And the inside doesn't disappoint either. With candles lit up beautifully,  dragon heads and buddhas it satisfies any traveller while you can watch the gongs outside being hit

Great place to relax and take shelter form harsh weather condition.It's very peaceful and quite beautiful, particularly on the inside. The temple is spacious and also has a little garden, with a lake and several tangerine trees.We got  there by taxi but you can also take bus 600 from Jeju International Airport (Bus Stop 1).

Beautiful quiet temple tucked away from the hustle of city life. expansive and breathtaking. There were prayers ongoing while we were there which were very relaxing to listen to just sitting quietly by. there's a little garden out in the front as well. Guests can arrange for a temple stay here too.
it's a bit off the beat but still quite a few tourists find their way but mainly by car or bus tour. Went there by bus which is still pretty easy.

Marado island is small island but it has amazing view. You can see the wide field, blue sea,and Jeju-representing rocks.You can borrow a bike and look around the island riding a bike. And there is also a good restaurants. They use Jeju local specialities.

We went to Marado Island by taking a 1 h-long ferry from Jeju Island (Daejung-Eup, Hamo ri). The ferry was nice and the could stand in either deck to enjoy the scenic view of the ocean. When you approach the island you could see the beauty of volcanic layers that forms the island and the interface of volcanic rocks and ocean was amazing. Walking is the best way to enjoy the island and you may spend nearly 3 h in the island. There are a couple of restaurants, a beautiful buddha temple, a church etc. A nice half-day trip. Highly recommended.

We went there by ferry, it takes around 1 hour, small but really nice island, must visit if you are in Jeju, it is the southern area of south Korea, population is only 90 , no cars aloud on the island you can make the whole tour by foot in 1 hour and a lot of beautiful scenery to see so prepare camera

Marado Island is remote, largely barren, and is "nearly" empty. There is a small population of island residents. There is a small oddly shaped church, a Buddhist temple, and a lighthouse. As far as buildings go, there is little of interest. The primary feature of Marado is the rugged coastline, typical of Jeju-do. Doesn't sound that appealing? Yet, I did enjoy my visit here because it is nice to see a part of Jeju that is largely unaffected by tourism, small museums, resorts, golf, or honeymooners. The ferry does not depart too frequently. Once you arrive on Marado, you really can only do one thing, walk around the entire island, which only takes 2 hours. If the weather is nice (May-August), you should be able to get some pretty pictures of the rugged coast, bright green grass, and some of the lonely buildings on the island.Some of these small island communities are such a contrast to our (foreigners) perception of Korea, that a visit in itself helps creates a more broad image of the country. A worthy experience, that I would recommend if you have plenty of time on Jeju Island.

Lee Jung-Seob Art Gallery, like most government run museums in Korea, had a low display items to museum area ratio.  It is dedicated to Lee who spent the last few years of his life in Seogwipo after being raised in present-day North Korea and spending a significant part of his life in Japan.  In a three floor building it was just one room with about 20 pieces of artifacts.  Fortunately the few artifacts which consisted of postcards Lee sent his wife, his earlier sketches, letters to his children, and his palette donated by his wife were all interesting to check out.
We visited this place and you can see the explanation of the art works while walking to this museum. Can visit for children to see =)
It was a great place to learn about history but not a must visit place. You can drop by or skip, if you have like one hour extra.

It is a museum showing the history of Korea, the emotions and aesthetics of Koreans. Lee joong seop died at a young age and did not leave much work. However, the well-maintained birthplace, street and cafés and crowds around them show how this artist is popularly loved by Koreans.

If you are in the Seogwipo-city area and only a short time in Je-Ju this is a great find. A traditional house, a story of a great S. Korean artist, a nicely designed park and a street of small arty shops.

LEE Joong Seop Street is lovely and there are some art shops where you can do window shopping. Then this small street lead you to the house where Lee's family lived for certain period, in a 4.6m2 room for 4 family member. You will be stunned to see how small it is!! But they loved this place where they could hug all the time, kids, and the couple. Behind those free zone, the art museum is located. Admission is 1,500 KRW(1.10 USD, 0.80 Euro). You can request docent on the spot. Korean is always ready, for English, better to call in advance when you will visit. At the end of the street, there is small traditional market where you can get some street food and fresh fruits. Strongly recommend to visit to feel the artist' spirits who lived miserable period. He made lots of work for 6 years before he died, age of 40's. It looks like Van Gogh did lots of works during short period. Good to visit 3rd floor to enjoy the view toward south part of Ocean.

actually we yet to go inside the museum but just walk around the street of LeeJoongSeop. not bad. however, seem that not too direct related to art but flea market or street market with some handmade stuff. if finish Seogwipo Maeil Olleh Market, go here together if you like to buy something.btw, it has an old cinemas but seem already closed. we saw a band to do some rehearsal. one of artist maybe

Was  a great refuge from a rainy day. Only one English sign so hard to know what it was all about. Artwork didn't appeal to me- seemed quite juvenile in style. Surrounding area is quite nice- coffee shops and stores.

I have a deep love and appreciation for the artist Lee Jung Seob. The museum itself  and the neighboring art-walk is a great tribute to the artist, but the exhibition itself does not do the artist that much justice. They have a great selection of his smaller works from the earlier periods but they do not house his bigger, dynamic paintings that he is known for. This visit would be a great place to take the family as the entrance fee is very manageable. The museum offers a closer look at the artists' context and life story rather than a display of his most prominent works. In short, a brilliant artist but not the best exhibition space/display method.

The museum is located next to a please area of town with multiple artists in various media as well as tea/coffee shops - which is how we found the location.  There is a small entrance fee (1000 Won per adult at the time).  In addition to the small, but nice collection of paintings and sculpture, there is a great view of the city and see from the 3rd floor.  If art is your thing, then definitely go.  Otherwise go only as weather or your schedule dictates.

Very talented artist and excellent works, a sad and interesting story. While the museum itself has only got a smallish collection, the park and the streets around the place is really worthwhile exploring, nice cafes and restaurants in the area too.
if you are an art lover you must go here. read a bit about the artist and his life before you visit.

He has quite a collection of his paintings exhibited in this museum.  If you have an eye for such artistic talent, then you would really appreciate this exhibits.  It is sad that a person has to die before his paintings can be recognized and treasured.  It would had been nice if his talent had been recognized earlier so he didn't have to be separated from his family.

It is very interesting - the museum is right next to the house where he used to live. And there is a painting that paints the view from the museum looking down the port. it is called "The view of the port" I believe the city of Seogwipo has bought this painting a few years ago and placed it in this museum - this is my favorite. The painter is a genius and of course ahead of his own time. I am proud and also feel bad for his personal life, just like any other genius who had a not so happy personal life and was too far ahead of everyone else. Enjoy great paintings. I am glad the city of Seogwipo is making efforts to keep his painting in the meaningful spot, not random museums elsewhere in the world.
